chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Respite your child until he reaches six years; then attach him to yourself for seven years, so discipline him with your discipline. So if he accepts and is correct, or else let him go.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended age-based approach to disciplining children in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a developmental framework where the first seven years focus on nurturing and play, while the subsequent seven years emphasize active moral instruction and discipline. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting parenting to the child's cognitive and emotional maturity, ensuring that training is effective before granting greater independence. This approach underscores the balance between affection and authority in raising a virtuous offspring.
